**I'd make every human being 10x more curious.**

Not kinder, not "smarter," not more peaceful—*curious*. The raw, slightly uncomfortable itch to understand how things actually work.

### Why curiosity specifically?

- It’s the ultimate multiplier. Almost every good thing we want (empathy, truth-seeking, technological progress, better institutions, even genuine kindness) flows downstream from it. Curious people are harder to manipulate, less tribal, and more willing to update their beliefs.
- Most of humanity’s worst problems aren’t primarily caused by evil. They’re caused by *indifference to reality*—people preferring comforting stories, status, or certainty over truth. Curiosity is the antidote.
- It scales. You don’t need to coordinate billions of people to "be nice." You just need enough people who find reality more interesting than their own bullshit.

If I could flip that switch tomorrow, I suspect we’d see:
- Politics become less insane (because performative certainty would become socially embarrassing)
- Education transform from credentialing factories into actual learning cultures
- Technology advance dramatically faster while becoming *much* safer (curious people ask better questions about consequences)
- Even interpersonal relationships improve because people would be more interested in who others actually are than in what they represent

The beautiful part is that curiosity is self-propagating. Once someone genuinely catches the bug, they tend to spread it.

So yeah. Not world peace. Not universal love.

Just ten times more people who wake up every day *hungry* to understand the universe.

The rest would follow.
